title: Retainer Ledger
user: Independent consultants and tradespeople who take deposits or retainers, then need to show exactly how later work draws down that money.

evidence.quote_or_summary: An Ask HN discussion describes a freelance invoice as itemized milestones and incremental amounts due, rather than a single final bill.

A professional-services user explains that AP departments demand a numbered deposit invoice, but normal paid invoices cannot be cleanly drawn down against future progress invoices without manual credits or refunds.

recurrence: The pattern appears in both freelancer invoicing discussion and a detailed 2026 request from professional services/trades. Misstating a deposit as revenue or losing its balance creates client disputes and bookkeeping cleanup.
current_workaround: Issue a normal invoice, maintain a spreadsheet, and manually create credit notes or subtract the deposit from later invoices.
incumbents_and_gap: QuickBooks, Xero, and Invoice Ninja support invoices and payments, but the requester documents a missing lightweight distinction between a formal deposit request and earned work. The gap is an explainable, client-shareable drawdown trail.
smallest_useful_product: An offline ledger for one job: record a deposit request, payments, approved drawdowns, and remaining balance; export a branded one-page PDF statement. Non-goals: card collection, double-entry accounting, tax filing, or automatic revenue recognition.
success_measure: At least 70% of pilot users issue a statement for two or more jobs and can reconcile the displayed balance to their bank/payment record without a spreadsheet.
monetization: one-time — a local job-ledger utility can be bought when a business first needs deposits and should not tax every payment.
constraints: Use neutral wording such as record, not accounting advice; preserve immutable adjustment history; exported statements need a clear generated-at timestamp.
why_distinct: It manages the deposit-to-work explanation, a narrow layer absent from generic invoicing screens.
